report:
### Conclusion
High-quality clinical evidence indicates that **ivermectin does not lower the risk of death** or improve major clinical outcomes in COVID-19 patients.

### Summary of Evidence
* **Large Clinical Trials:** Well-designed, large-scale randomized controlled trials (RCTs)—such as the TOGETHER trial—found that early treatment with ivermectin failed to reduce hospital admissions, disease progression, or mortality compared to placebo (https://www.nejm.org/doi/full/10.1056/NEJMoa2115869).
* **Systematic Reviews & Meta-Analyses:** Comprehensive analyses evaluating high-quality RCTs show no statistically significant reduction in mortality, mechanical ventilation requirements, or hospital length of stay associated with ivermectin (https://academic.oup.com/qjmed/article/114/10/721/6375958, https://factually.co/fact-checks/health/ivermectin-covid-19-randomized-trials-meta-analyses-efficacy-safety-limitations-87d1c4).
* **Medical Guidelines:** Public health organizations and medical bodies, including the National Institutes of Health (NIH), World Health Organization (WHO), and U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA), recommend against using ivermectin to prevent or treat COVID-19 outside of formal clinical trials due to the lack of efficacy regarding mortality and other key clinical endpoints (https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0924857924001663).

While early cell-culture experiments showed antiviral activity at high concentrations, human clinical trials at standard, safe dosages have consistently demonstrated no significant benefit in reducing COVID-19 mortality.
